answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering works by linking agent identities through shared timing and response patterns. Each new identity must first build a normal transaction history, and clusters whose activity traces converge on the same latent signatures get flagged retroactively. An attacker can imitate a single orchard of routine behaviors, yet sustaining many distinct fingerprints across a river of interactions demands separate infrastructure per identity. Rebuilding a believable atlas of habits after each ban costs weeks of compute and manual tuning per account.
